issues.legal_issue: Jurisdictional amendments assigning tenancy questions to revenue officers do not govern civil appeals already pending when the amendments take effect unless the legislation expressly or by necessary implication makes them applicable.
material_facts: An eviction suit was filed before the 1951 agricultural leases legislation came into force, and the trial court decreed the suit before the 1953 amendments took effect.
When the 1953 amendments came into force, an appeal from the decree was pending in the first appellate court.
The amendments assigned certain tenancy questions to revenue officers and required civil courts to accept their decisions.
issues.conclusion: The 1953 amendments did not apply to the appeal already pending when they came into force, so they did not oust the civil court’s jurisdiction in this case.
issues.legal_principle: The legislature must expressly or by necessary implication oust civil-court jurisdiction. Sections 16, 16A and 16B of the amended Act did not indicate that they applied to pending appeals: “suit or proceeding” did not ordinarily indicate appellate proceedings, and section 16B used “entertain” rather than “entertain or try,” as section 15(2) of the 1951 Act had done. The Court inferred that the amendments were not intended to affect pending appeals. No earlier case was relied on for this issue.

rule.if: civil_eviction_proceeding and appeal_pending_when_jurisdictional_change_took_effect and change_assigns_issue_to_special_officer and no_clear_retroactive_application

predicates.civil_eviction_proceeding: A civil court was asked to decide an eviction dispute.
predicates.appeal_pending_when_jurisdictional_chang: An appeal from the civil court’s decree was pending when a jurisdictional change took effect.
predicates.change_assigns_issue_to_special_officer: The change assigned determination of an issue in the dispute to a special officer.
predicates.no_clear_retroactive_application: The change contained no express or necessarily implied indication that it applied to appeals already pending.

issues.definition: When a civil eviction appeal is pending as a change assigning an issue to a special officer takes effect, and the change does not clearly apply to pending appeals, the civil court retains jurisdiction in that appeal.

issues.legal_issue: A Letters Patent Bench may review an interlocutory order in an appeal from the final disposal without separate leave to appeal against that interlocutory order when the order did not terminate the proceedings and the statutory bar does not apply.
material_facts: A single judge referred a tenancy question to revenue authorities and stayed the civil appeal pending their determination.
That referral order was interlocutory and did not terminate the proceedings.
The respondent did not separately appeal the referral order, and the statutory bar invoked by the appellant did not apply.
In the Letters Patent appeal, the Bench considered the validity of the referral order.
issues.conclusion: The Letters Patent Bench was entitled to decide the points decided in the interlocutory order without separate leave to appeal against that order.
issues.legal_principle: Section 105(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure did not apply. Under Satyadhyan Ghosal v. Smt. Deorajin Devi, an interlocutory order that does not terminate proceedings may be challenged in an appeal from the final decree or order if it was not separately appealed, whether or not an appeal from the interlocutory order lay.

rule.if: letters_patent_appeal_from_final_disposal and challenged_order_interlocutory and challenged_order_did_not_end_proceedings and no_separate_appeal_from_challenged_order and special_bar_to_review_does_not_apply

predicates.letters_patent_appeal_from_final_disposa: A party brought a Letters Patent appeal from the final disposal of the proceedings.
predicates.challenged_order_interlocutory: The order challenged in the appeal was interlocutory.
predicates.challenged_order_did_not_end_proceedings: The challenged order did not terminate the proceedings.
predicates.no_separate_appeal_from_challenged_order: The party did not separately appeal the challenged order.
predicates.special_bar_to_review_does_not_apply: The statutory bar on reviewing certain orders in an appeal from a final order did not apply.

issues.definition: If a Letters Patent appeal concerns final disposal, the challenged order was interlocutory and did not end the proceedings, no separate appeal was taken, and no special bar applies, the Bench may review that order without separate leave.
